clips.title: The story
paras: Camping 101: Skinning is an introductory wilderness instruction given to novice gatherers in Tirisfal Glades and across Azeroth. It directs skinners who have practiced their trade to regional craftsmen to learn how to fashion a durable camp chair out of harvested hides.

Survival in the wilds demands more than a sharp blade; it requires knowing how to husband your strength between trials. Adventurers like Eleanor Shackleton emphasize that harvesting beast pelts provides more than raw trade goods. By developing basic field proficiency, skinners can fashion essential camp comforts like chairs out of treated skins, allowing weary wanderers to rest and recover properly before their next perilous encounter.

In Tirisfal Glades, young Forsaken skinners who reach initial competency are pointed toward Rand Rhobart, who plies his trade along the road linking Brill to the Capital ruins of the Undercity. Rhobart shares practical techniques for turning rough leather into functional campsite seating, an art mirrored by skinning masters throughout the lands of both the Horde and the Alliance.

clips.title: Quest text
paras: Being able to skillfully harvest the skins and hides of fallen beasts is one of the more valuable skills an adventurer can possess.

I reckon I know someone that can teach you how to craft a Camp Chair for your camp. Sometimes it's important to just take a load off, and you can use some of those hides you've gathered to make a comfy chair to sit in. A bit of relaxation can help ensure that you are at your peak condition and can strike where it counts the next time you find yourself in a dust-up.

clips.title: Progress
paras: Ah yes, I can teach you.

clips.title: Completion
paras: There you have it, you can now craft your very own Camp Chair. Most folk don't care much for camps being set up in the center of town, so you'll need to head into the wilderness if you want to test it out.

Oh, and just remember, no camp is complete without a campfire. You'll need one of those before you start up your camp. Most cooks can teach you to make a fire. If you haven't already, you might want to check in with someone who can train you in the culinary arts to learn the basics.
